Trying it at adb speed skipped to the next episode and seeked (S08E05 -> S08E06, position 740 -> 1127) instead of exiting. KEYCODE_MEDIA_STOP exits cleanly in one key.

step: CORRECTION to the exit-playback entry (16:07)
what_happened: The earlier entry said the HUD 'auto-hides while the user is walking its controls'. That is wrong: playback_screen._handleKey calls service.showOverlay() for every key while the HUD is visible, which restarts the 4 s window. Re-reading the evidence: each adb screencap takes ~2-3 s, so the HUD hid because I paused to capture between presses, not because input failed to reset the timer.
expected: the ledger states what was actually measured
verdict: CORRECTION. The real defect is the 4-second window itself (see next entry), and the design escalation must use the corrected fact so K3.1 is not asked to fix a non-bug.

step: exit playback: why presses turn into seeks
what_happened: While the HUD is hidden, Left/Right are seek keys (a deliberate design: seek without waking the HUD). The HUD hides 4 s after the last input. An exit walk is 5 presses plus human hesitation, so pressing Right just after the window lapsed seeks instead of moving focus: in one measured attempt the position jumped 740 s -> 1127 s and the episode changed. So the same key means 'move focus' or 'seek 10 s' depending on a timer the viewer cannot see.
expected: arrows always mean one thing while the viewer is in control of the HUD, and the exit cost is the same every time
verdict: OPEN, design decision pending K3.1 (provider down, three failed attempts). Candidate directions: longer idle window, a persistent visible hint that arrows seek while hidden, and a one-press exit affordance.
evidence: screenshots /tmp/exit1.png (overlay visible, Back focused), /tmp/exit3.png (overlay hidden after ~4 s), DB position 740 -> 1127 and episode 781 -> 782

step: the 5-press exit walk, measured cleanly (all keys within one second)

Result: instead of leaving playback the client opened the NEXT episode, Archer S08E07 'Gramercy, Halberd!', and resumed it at its stored position 805 s. So the focus path from the top bar reaches the skip-next control, and Select on it starts different content than the viewer was watching.
expected: the same 5 presses leave playback and save the place, every time
verdict: OPEN — P1 class: an attempt to exit can switch episodes (wrong content, stale position) with no confirmation. Precise focus graph must come from the K3.1 spec; candidate constraint regardless of design: Select must never start different content while the viewer is trying to leave.
evidence: screenshot /tmp/exitwalk.png (S08E07 at 13:19); DB PlaybackProgress 783 position 805 updated 17:27:41; sequence sent via one adb 'input keyevent 4 19 22 22 23'

Root cause of the retry not working at first: two concurrent stopScan() calls awaited the same subscription cancel and never completed — fixed in DiscoveryService.stopScan.

step: the embedded-track sweep: throughput and two self-inflicted traps
what_happened: The first three sweeps cleared the newest 120 files (about 1,100 subtitle tracks, zero failures) but left 2,798 files unpicked, which at 40 per pass is ~12 hours. Raised to 150 per pass (ffprobe is a child process; the pass owns a 10-minute slot) -> 1,409 then 893 tracks per pass. Two traps found by measuring rather than assuming: (a) files with NO embedded subtitle streams stay in the 'no EMBEDDED rows' set for ever, so the sweep would re-probe them every ten minutes - fixed with a probe-state file (/config/embedded-track-sweep.json keyed by variant id + size/mtime); (b) those trackless files are the newest ids, so a flat LIMIT returned the same 150 candidates every pass and the sweep could never advance - fixed by walking down in id chunks and skipping probed ids before the limit.

The keyring was reachable all along once `secretstorage` was installed for the Python that runs yt-dlp, and `--cookies-from-browser chrome+gnomekeyring` extracts the same stream successfully.

The YouTube library keeps every previously downloaded video playable; new downloads resume at the next 20-minute cycle.

step: the server froze for 170 seconds while the TV was watching

Cause is load, not one bug: (a) the full-library sidecar sweep ran ~3,700 variants / ~7,600 track rows without yielding; (b) embedded subtitle extraction (which my new embedded-track rows feed) doubled subtitle-sync's candidate set from 729 to ~1,650 sidecars, so a 10-candidate sync cycle took 11-14 minutes of its 15-minute slot; (c) six heavy passes all started on the same minutes (*/10 and */15 collide at :00 and :30) on a 4-core box, so ffmpeg/ffprobe jobs bunched up.
